comparisons.interpretation: Both connect unsafe conversions to affordability and tenant protection. El-Yateem foregrounds affordable construction and stronger accountability; Brannan specifies a relocation fund financed by landlord fines. These tools can coexist.

El-Yateem specifies affordable replacement housing alongside accountability; Carroll specifies judicially authorized inspections. The selected answers do not establish that either rejects the other's measure.
Both explicitly propose more affordable homes for people otherwise displaced from unsafe conversions and reject treating fines alone as a sufficient remedy.

El-Yateem conditions bike-share support on preserving parking; Brannan favors waterfront recreation while doubting transportation utility. Both have qualified positions, not a simple pro-bike versus anti-bike split.
El-Yateem emphasizes a no-parking-loss condition; Carroll emphasizes community participation in siting. These requirements are not inherently incompatible.

Both raise parking and siting concerns. El-Yateem makes retaining parking an explicit condition; Tong additionally emphasizes resident polling and rider safety. Her question about siting is not silently converted into an identical veto.
Both argue taxpaying private-street residents deserve garbage collection. Brannan emphasizes litigation while El-Yateem describes service restoration and public outreach.
Both support garbage collection for private-street taxpayers; Tong specifies smaller trucks as a practical tool.

El-Yateem argues for collection based on taxpayer status. Carroll explicitly declines truck access while a street remains unmapped and proposes curbside disposal instead. This is a stated condition on service rather than an invented general opposition to sanitation.

Both explicitly oppose supervised injection facilities in these2017 interviews and favor counseling or treatment. The DSA endorsement is not used to infer the reverse position, and these statements are not clinical recommendations.
Both affirm counseling and treatment resources. This agreement is limited to that tool: Carroll's quoted answer does not establish agreement with El-Yateem's separate opposition to injection sites.

El-Yateem foregrounds counseling, treatment and family engagement; Brannan foregrounds prevention, stigma reduction and child education. No direct injection-site disagreement is coded because Brannan's position on that detail appears only in reporter paraphrase here.

El-Yateem foregrounds inclusion and resistance to attacks on civil liberties; Carroll presents a moderate cross-party community representative. This does not imply El-Yateem refuses cross-party cooperation; his separate email interview explicitly endorses it.

El-Yateem foregrounds inclusive community leadership and civil-liberties resistance; Brannan describes municipal constituent service as activism. The evidence does not support labeling Brannan simply anti-activist.

El-Yateem foregrounds inclusion and civil-liberties leadership; Tong foregrounds constituent work and personal outreach over publicity. These are stated emphases, not measurements of how much either campaign advertised.
